newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end higher, seen on upward track. [CORRECTED 10:10 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end higher, seen on upward track. [CORRECTED 10:10 GMT]

text.p: Singapore shares rallied on Tuesday closing firmer and giving hope to dealers that the market was back on an upward track for at least the near term.
"The market has recovered from the recent travel down and we're back to a better level," said a local dealer.
"I think we're getting back towards a better run," he added.

Singapore's benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) closed up 22.27 points at 2,194.75, helping the index towards the 2,200 resistance level analysts see as a key barrier. (Corrects rise and closing values from "18.55 points at 2,191.03" to "22.27 points at 2,194.75")
Traded volume was 247.1 million shares, producing 267 gainers against 112 losers.
Blue chips Fraser & Neave, up Singapore $0.50 to S$13.30, and Cycle & Carriage, up S$0.60 to S$15.00, were the stocks responsible for most of the STII's rebound, dealers said.
Gainers were led by Singapore Press foreign stock up $0.70 at S$28.70, with see-saw electronic stock Creative Technology topping the losers, down S$1.20 at S$16.10.
Keppel FELS, the shipyard unit of Keppel Corp, also saw a hard fall, dropping S$0.60 to S$5.15 after the company said its outlook for 1997 was poor.
